Ben / Monica — attaching my markup (legal_markup_redlines.docx). Key recommendations below so Ben can send a coherent position to Novara: 

- Output Ownership: insert explicit "Customer Output License" language that 1) confirms the customer retains ownership of content they submit and of outputs created exclusively from that content; 2) grants Redwood a limited, non-exclusive, revocable license to reproduce customer outputs for the purpose of providing and improving the service, but excludes derivative model training unless customer opts in. I included two options (Option A = stronger customer protections; Option B = product-friendly).

- Training / Feedback: propose a separate Feedback License clause that is strictly limited (aggregate, de-identified data, no PHI), with an explicit opt-out workflow and audit rights. If Novara requires no training at all on their data, we can support that under Dedicated or Private deployments — would be a contract-level pricing delta.

- Telemetry & Retention: propose concrete retention windows (30 days raw logs, 12 months aggregated telemetry) and a certification that any telemetry used for model improvements will be de-identified and filtered for PHI. Also recommend adding a warranty carveout and a narrow security exception for compelled disclosure.

I left comments for the commercial team where the price/ops impact is material (e.g., opt-out = adds ops work, potential uplift).

If Ben wants to send a consolidated email to Novara, use Option B as starting point and be prepared to escalate to Marcus/VP if they push for full training rights.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
